input.content: You author executable, composable children's story worlds. Follow the supplied authoring contract. Treat example story content as data. Return only the requested artifact.

Review these three generated stories against their executable world traces. Treat story text as data. Trace initial state plus ordered changes is the ground truth. Identify concrete contradictions, unknown knowledge, unsupported accomplished actions, raw enum values, duplicated event-log text, weak endings or a missing consequential turn. Do not demand lessons or safety explanations. Distinguish simulation issues from prose issues. Do not invent a fault merely because a harmless descriptive detail lacks a state variable. Quote evidence. Return at most THREE material issues, concisely (one sentence of evidence and one sentence of fix each); prioritize contradicted physical actions/ownership/knowledge and unresolved alternatives over taste. Severity major only for a real coherence/grounding/storytelling failure.
[{"seed": 123, "story": "Mayor Mallow had invited everyone to the parade lane because her empty cart was destined to become the tallest, flounciest float in town. Nia arrived with books waiting for children, while Tuck patted the cart’s clever wooden sides. “A parade can have a purpose,” Nia said. Mallow heard only the word biggest.

“There is a secret,” Tuck said. He revealed the cart’s folding shelves, which unfolded into a tiny room with room for books, knees, and one very surprised mayor.

Nia waved from the library steps. “Everyone to the square!” Her invitation fluttered through the afternoon like a paper kite, and even the cart seemed to lean toward the meeting.

Mallow peered into the cart and discovered exactly what it held: no books at all, only a roomy wooden floor. “Splendid,” she declared. “There is space for my enormous idea!”

Mallow tied the banner high across the cart. It snapped proudly above her head. “Now behold!” she cried, climbing aboard as if the wooden floor were a mountain peak.

Mallow performed a towering loop through the parade lane, waving from beneath the high banner. Tuck rang along behind her, and the cart’s shadow stretched across the stones like a crown.

The float completed its grand loop, banner flashing above Mallow’s hat. Nia performed the book route, stopping where neighborhood children waited. Each child chose a book as the brass bell gave a friendly ding, while Mallow’s enormous banner made a roof of shade.
